solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What'll bind dunes on open beaches, initially at least

definitions.text: What'll bind dunes on open beaches, initially at least

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the four words dunes, on, open, beaches

parts.note: the four words read straight, their leading letters giving the answer

explanation.surface: A coastal planter asks which grass will hold sand dunes in place on exposed beaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: doob is a creeping grass, and 'at least' hedges that it is one of several such binders.
explanation.definitionFit: Doob, or Bermuda grass, is a creeping turf grass with long runners, the kind planted to stabilise loose sand.

clue.text: Rookies trained to ultimate in endeavour, i.e. on square

indicators.note: letters that are trained are drilled into a new order, so the pieces are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the final letter of endeavour

parts.note: the word endeavour, whose last letter is used
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for square, as in sq. or S on maps and measures

explanation.surface: Novices are drilled to do their utmost, squaring up to the task.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiroes is Chambers's plural of tiro, a variant spelling of tyro.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiro is a beginner or novice, the same idea as a rookie in a new job or team.

clue.text: Brief affairs providing kicks

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a fling is a kick or sudden throw of the limbs, as by a horse

explanation.surface: Short romances give people their thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicks' looks like thrills to go with the affairs, but it is the literal sense of lashing out with the legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fling is a casual romance and also a plunging kick or throw of the body, as a horse gives.

clue.text: Night flyer maybe making cock-up, velocity constant

parts.note: a booboo is a blunder, the same as a cock-up
velocity constant is an older name for the rate constant in chemistry, written k

explanation.surface: A pilot flying at night makes a mess of things while holding a steady speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Night flyer' suggests a pilot, but it is an owl. The rate of a chemical reaction was once called its velocity constant, symbol k.
explanation.definitionFit: The boobook is a small Australasian owl, a nocturnal bird named from its call.

clue.text: Shower of missiles when alongside Troy? He'd only a light shield

parts.note: a pelt is a volley of thrown things, as in a pelting
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
t is the abbreviation for troy, the weight system used for precious metals

explanation.surface: Missiles rain down at Troy, and the warrior has nothing but a flimsy shield.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy suggests the Greek siege, but here it is the troy weight abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A peltast was a light infantryman of ancient Greece, carrying a small crescent-shaped shield called a pelta.

clue.text: Happening on one cupola he's put up in sheltered housing? (12, two words)

parts.note: an event is something that happens

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the cupola

parts.note: a dome is a rounded roof such as a cupola

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means he is turned to read bottom to top

parts.note: he's taken as the word he

explanation.surface: Someone describes an event with a domed building going up as part of a housing scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that 'sheltered housing' is a description by example rather than a strict synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventide home is a residential home for elderly people, a kind of sheltered accommodation.

clue.text: Refuse receptacle (12, two words)

definitions.meaning: read as the noun for rubbish, not the verb to decline
a container, here one put out for people's waste

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word, given by a plain definition alone: entrants wrote their own clues for it, so there is no wordplay to find.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter basket is a bin in a street or park for people to drop their rubbish into.

clue.text: Expression of e.g. grief captured in paintings, say, in disorderly style

indicators.note: captured in places the cry inside the word for paintings

parts.note: paintings are an example of art
io is an old exclamation of grief or triumph

explanation.surface: A painter's work captures sorrow in a wild, chaotic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Io is a Greek and Latin interjection, used in English for joy or lament.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariot means in a riot, running wild or in unruly confusion, an adverb of disorder.

clue.text: Broken nibs pocketed where unruly pupils go (6, two words)

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
a pocketed ball is in, as in snooker or pool

explanation.surface: A child snaps pen nibs and gets sent off for misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin bin is a room or unit where badly behaved schoolchildren are sent, borrowed from the sports penalty area.

clue.text: Explosive TNT on it explodes, but only partly

indicators.note: but only partly says just a portion of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: the answer runs across 'tNT ON IT Explodes'

explanation.surface: Dynamite placed on something only half goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explodes' looks like an anagram signal, but it is merely part of the text the answer runs through.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonite is a blasting compound made from guncotton and barium nitrate, used in quarrying.

clue.text: Muscular sheet seen in transatlantic fish, S. Am. possibly

parts.note: the platy is a small Central American freshwater fish, popular in aquaria

indicators.note: possibly lets the letters of S. Am. take another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sheet of muscle turns up in a fish from across the Atlantic, perhaps from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S. Am.' looks like the abbreviation for South America, fitting the fish, but it is only three letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The platysma is the broad thin layer of muscle in the neck that tenses the skin and draws down the mouth.

clue.text: See variety turn and frivol with it idly? Highly corrosive stuff (12, three words)

indicators.note: turn means the variety word is read from its end backwards

parts.note: an olio is a miscellany or variety show

indicators.note: idly says the letters are fooled about with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch a music-hall act twist and play about idly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety turn' reads as a music-hall act, but the variety is an olio and 'turn' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil of vitriol is the old name for concentrated sulphuric acid, a strongly corrosive liquid.

clue.text: Number one run out after reverse sweep belted one

indicators.note: a reverse sweep plays the ball the opposite way, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the top batsman is run out after playing a reverse sweep and hitting the ball hard.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse sweep is a cricket stroke played across the body the wrong way. 'Belted one' sounds like a big hit but means a figure wearing a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion the hunter is the constellation famous for the three stars forming his belt.

clue.text: Scots won't delay disposing of it round pub

indicators.note: round puts the remaining letters about the pub
disposing of means the word it is dropped from the word for delay

parts.note: to wait is to delay or hold back
taken as written
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A Scot refuses to put off getting rid of something near the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Winna is the Scots contraction of will not, used where English speakers say won't.

clue.text: Old-fashioned cracker, note wrapped inside gift

indicators.note: wrapped inside puts the note within the gift, as a present holds its contents

parts.note: a boon is a gift or blessing
NB, nota bene, is a written note to take heed

explanation.surface: A traditional Christmas cracker hides a little message inside the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' suggests a musical letter, but it is NB, the reminder written in margins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonbon was once a name for a Christmas cracker, the paper tube pulled at parties.

clue.text: Cheap US book, apocryphal, about Washington

indicators.note: about places the Tobit book around the state abbreviation

parts.note: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha
W is the US postal-style abbreviation for Washington

explanation.surface: A cheap American paperback of dubious authority covers George Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apocrypha are the Old Testament books outside the Hebrew canon; Tobit is one.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang two-bit means worth a quarter-dollar, hence cheap, petty or second-rate.

clue.text: Generated billion I turned as clear profit

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I

indicators.note: turned reverses the word for clear profit

parts.note: nett is profit after all deductions

explanation.surface: A financier boasts of producing a billion that he converted into pure profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Begotten is the past participle of beget, to father or bring into being, much like produced.

clue.text: Kt ran pub chaotically — becoming so?

definitions.text: Kt ran pub chaotically — becoming so?

indicators.note: chaotically signals the letters are thrown into disorder and reassembled

parts.note: Kt, the abbreviation for knight, plus ran and pub, give eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A knight ran a pub so badly that it went bust.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: a pub run chaotically by a knight is heading for insolvency. Kt is the abbreviation for knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankrupt describes a business or person legally unable to pay debts, the fate of a mismanaged pub.

clue.text: Infatuate old fool with love alongside famous model

definitions.note: an obsolete verb, so 'old' marks the archaic word

parts.note: an ass is a fool
love is zero in tennis, written O
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: An old fool in love takes up with a celebrated fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous model' hints at a catwalk star, but it is Ford's Model T car.
explanation.definitionFit: Assot is an archaic verb meaning to besot or make foolishly devoted.

clue.text: French town (historically) is rolling

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capital of Brittany
second meaning: an old form of runs, as a wheel or river runs

explanation.surface: A French town in the past was thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: Renne is an obsolete spelling of run, so rennes is the old third-person form.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennes is the Breton city, and in archaic English it was the form of runs, meaning moves along continuously.

clue.text: Hypothetical evolutionary 'force' deployed in murines

indicators.note: deployed means the letters are spread out and arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theoretical evolutionary drive is found at work in mice and rats.
explanation.walkthrough: Murines are rodents of the mouse family, a fitting place to look for evolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurism was a proposed nerve force once thought to drive evolutionary change.

clue.text: Get gloomier, having to change ends, annoyed

indicators.note: to change ends swaps the first and last letters of the word for growing gloomy

parts.note: to darken is to grow dim or gloomy

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more miserable when forced to swap ends of the pitch, and is irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change ends' sounds like teams at half-time; here the two end letters trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: Narked is British slang for irritated or fed up.

clue.text: Moroccan tree marking site of famous anchorage?

parts.note: the arar is the sandarac tree of north-west Africa
at is the preposition that marks a place, as in at home

explanation.surface: A North African tree marks where a well-known harbour lies.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the joke: the famous anchorage is Noah's Ark coming to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat in Turkey is where, in Genesis, Noah's Ark came to rest after the Flood.

clue.text: Rule, what led to Zimbabwe, gutted Smith, rather uncultured

parts.note: UDI, the Unilateral Declaration of Independence, broke Rhodesia from Britain on the road to Zimbabwe

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides of Smith, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Smith with its middle letters removed

explanation.surface: A history note: the regime that preceded Zimbabwe, and a crushed Ian Smith, look rather crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Smith led Rhodesia's white minority government, which declared UDI in 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens rude, so rudish means somewhat rough, coarse or unrefined.

clue.text: Sort of pouch Yank has inside part of nice cummerbund

definitions.note: Yank flags the American spelling of the word

indicators.note: has inside part of says the answer is a stretch of letters within the following words

parts.note: the answer runs across 'niCE CUMmerbund'

explanation.surface: An American wears a cummerbund with a little pocket tucked into it.
explanation.walkthrough: British spelling has caecum; 'Yank' signals the American form.
explanation.definitionFit: The cecum is the blind pouch at the start of the large intestine, the American spelling of caecum.

clue.text: Epileptic spasm? Responsibility follows aimless assertion

indicators.note: follows places the responsibility after the shortened assertion
aimless says the word aim is to be removed from the assertion

parts.note: a claim is an assertion
onus is a burden of responsibility

explanation.surface: A medical query about a seizure leads into a vague claim about who is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Clonus is a series of rapid muscle contractions and relaxations, as seen in some seizures.

clue.text: Strife dividing pud shifted to higher things

indicators.note: dividing puts the conflict in the middle, splitting the other letters
shifted means the letters of pud are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
war is conflict or strife

explanation.surface: A quarrel over the pudding is moved to loftier matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Upward is an adverb of direction, meaning toward a higher place or level.

clue.text: Porker in season gobbles this swill

indicators.note: gobbles says the phrase swallows the answer within its letters

parts.note: the answer runs across 'porkeR IN SEason'

explanation.surface: A pig in its season wolfs down the slop in its trough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swill' is the pig food the surface suggests, but it is a verb, to wash out.
explanation.definitionFit: To swill something is to wash it out with plenty of water, which is exactly what rinsing does.

clue.text: Map a clue wrongly — admission of guilt (8, two words)

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are put together in the wrong, rearranged order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter confesses to drawing up a clue badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is Latin for 'through my fault', used as an acknowledgement of one's error.

clue.text: What's served up at the Academy? It's often not cooked

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London
a dish is food served at table

explanation.surface: Someone asks what's on the menu at the Academy, and is told it's usually raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' suggests a reversal, but it simply means the food that is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Radishes are root vegetables usually eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Strangely cross about women's writings

indicators.note: about wraps the rearranged letters around the women's letter
strangely says the letters of cross come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Someone is oddly angry about what women have written.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrow is an old word for a scroll or written document, so scrows are writings.

clue.text: Female name for emotional therapy?

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a woman's name to give to a kind of feelings-based therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shen is a form of body therapy that claims to release painful feelings held in the body.

clue.text: We all pass this joyless trip, myself included

indicators.note: included puts the speaker inside what remains
joyless says the letters of joy are removed from the trip

parts.note: a journey is a trip
I is the setter speaking of himself

explanation.surface: Everyone must take this cheerless journey, the speaker too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' sounds like passing through life; the earthy sense of passing water is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Urine is the bodily waste that everyone passes, a euphemistic and accurate definition.

clue.text: Independence in writing style recalled e.g. Sheridan?

indicators.note: in puts independence inside the turned word
recalled means the writing word is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: your hand is your handwriting

explanation.surface: A literary note on independence in the style of the playwright Sheridan.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheridan suggests the dramatist Richard Brinsley Sheridan, but it is the actress Dinah Sheridan of The Railway Children.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinah Sheridan was a British film actress, so she is an example of someone bearing this first name.

clue.text: Dad's sudden fit, once, clutching me in old dance

parts.note: pa's is the possessive of pa, father

indicators.note: clutching holds the word me inside the old seizure word

parts.note: seasure is an old spelling of seizure
taken as written

explanation.surface: Father had a seizure in the past while gripping the speaker during an old-fashioned dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Seasure is an obsolete spelling of seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: The passamezzo or passemeasure was a lively Italian dance of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Staggering tot has inserted her logarithm base in addition

indicators.note: has inserted puts her and the base inside the rearranged tot
staggering means the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A wobbling toddler is shown her logarithms as an extra lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: e, about 2.718, is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is a formal adverb meaning besides or as well as that.
